expectedFindings.expectedMeaning: For a fixed amount and composition of gas under the stated gas-law model, pressure, volume and temperature are dependent state parameters. Changing one requires at least one other to adjust, not necessarily both. An experimental constraint can keep another parameter constant.
reject: Saying that changing one parameter forces every other parameter to change.
Leaving fixed gas amount implicit in the repaired introductory dependence statement.
Treating changing parameters as a phase-transition definition.

expectedMeaning: A thermodynamic state is a condition described by state parameters. A process connects states.
For the gas discussed here, an isothermal process changes thermodynamic state while the gas temperature remains unchanged.
An isothermal process is not, by definition, restricted to gaseous matter. Keep any remains-gas statement explicitly confined to this Boyle-law gas context.

The two labelled pressure-volume states belong to the same amount of gas at the same temperature; the comparison is between individual thermodynamic states, not between phases or between temperatures.

A physical phase change means a change such as gas becoming liquid. This Boyle-law comparison assumes the sample stays gaseous, without turning that assumption into a definition of all isothermal processes.
expectedFindings.reservoirQualification: Source-attribute the textbook's heat-exchange account. Effective thermal contact and sufficiently slow change can maintain approximately constant gas temperature in this model. Stable surrounding-air temperature alone is not a guarantee, and a reservoir is not an unqualified universal necessity in the definition.
